# Implementation Plan: Fix crews proactive-terminal-report deliver/consume silent-loss race
<!-- ralph-meta {"overviewTaskId":"crews-proactive-done-auto-consumed-silent-lead-miss"} -->

*Generated by `/plan-with-ralph` on 2026-06-05. Ready for `/implement-with-ralph --from-plan D:/harness-efforts/codexu/.ralph/jobs/crews-proactive-done-auto-consumed-silent-lead-miss/plan.md`. Revised after a 3-way multi-model Phase-4 review (Claude + Codex + Copilot) — see the review-findings appendix at the bottom.*

## Overview

A member's proactive terminal report (`kind=done|question|blocked`, `routingKind=proactive-report`) routed to the lead's mailbox is intermittently consumed at delivery and silently lost: `consumedAt` is stamped ~immediately after `writtenAt`, `mailbox.json` is left empty, the review-required cursor advances, and NO lead `system_notification` fires (reproduced live 2026-06-05 at lead `overview-bookkeeper` mailbox-history seq 379). The dominant root cause is an **orphan/duplicate listener subprocess race**: `markArmIntent` (PreToolUse) nulls `lastListenerPid`, which defeats the `requireFreshArm` already-active-listener guard in the next listener's `markArmed` (the guard requires `Number.isInteger(lastListenerPid)`), so two same-session listener subprocesses go live. `consumeMailbox`'s session fence rejects only a *different* session, so the orphan can win the mailbox lock and drain. One listener drains + exits with `{type:messages}` on its own stdout while the runtime is awaiting a *different* (newer) listener subprocess — that notification is dropped — and the live listener then drains an empty mailbox and never notifies. A secondary loss path is the Stop-hook opportunistic-consume TOCTOU (`stop.js` consumes when `listenerState !== 'armed'`).

The fix makes "which listener subprocess is allowed to drain the mailbox" a **precise, monotonic ownership check** rather than a PID-equality guess. It introduces a per-actor monotonic **listener epoch** (generation token): each successful `markArmed` bumps the epoch and records the arming listener's PID; the listener subprocess remembers the epoch it was granted and passes it to `consumeMailbox`, which refuses (returns `[]`) when the caller is not the current-epoch listener — validated **atomically under the manifest lock** so no concurrent `markArmed` can interleave between the check and the drain commit. A prevention layer (only a new listener's `markArmed` ever writes/overwrites `lastListenerPid`; neither `markArmIntent` nor `markExited` nulls it) keeps the `requireFreshArm` guard effective so duplicate listeners are rarely created in the first place. Together these give a **provable guarantee**: a queued proactive report is either delivered (and notified) by the current-epoch listener, or left queued for it — a superseded/orphan listener is always refused and never consumes-and-drops. The 3-way review showed a bare PID fence does NOT achieve this (an orphan that still owns `lastListenerPid` would pass it); the epoch makes the guarantee hold.

The fix is engine-independent, so it is resilient to the codex 125→135 hook-cadence change the operator flagged as a likely aggravator (more PreToolUse `markArmIntent` calls → more duplicate-listener windows). It ships as a crews patch release via the two-commit toolkit-submodule flow (submodule commit + codexu pointer-bump commit, including the root AGENTS.md active-plugin-versions CI-invariant table) and must serialize after the in-flight `impl-d001-toolkit-guard` (both touch crews release-stamp files; code edit sites are disjoint).

## Approach

### Architecture
Make the right-to-drain a precise, monotonic ownership check, in two complementary layers:

- **Ownership layer (containment — guarantees no silent loss):** add a per-actor monotonic `lastListenerEpoch`. `markArmed` bumps it (under the manifest lock) ONLY on a genuine arm transition (arming PID differs from the current `lastListenerPid`, or no epoch yet) and records the arming PID; same-listener heartbeat refreshes do NOT bump it. The listener subprocess captures the epoch it was granted (from its own first `markArmed`) and passes `{ sessionId, listenerPid, listenerEpoch }` to `consumeMailbox` for the rest of its lifetime. `consumeMailbox` performs the ownership check **under the manifest lock, atomically with committing the drain**: if the caller's epoch is not the current `manifest.lastListenerEpoch` (i.e. a newer listener has armed since), it refuses — returns `[]`, writes no history row, leaves `mailbox.json` unchanged, and logs `listener-orphan-consume-refused`. Because the epoch read and the drain-commit are serialized under the same manifest lock that `markArmed` uses to bump the epoch, the F-002 TOCTOU (a `markArmed` write interleaving between the check and the drain) is closed. The PID is retained as a secondary signal but the epoch is the authoritative ownership token.
- **Prevention layer (reduces duplicate-listener frequency):** unify `lastListenerPid` ownership so only a *new listener's* `markArmed` ever writes it (to its own PID); neither `markArmIntent` nor `markExited` nulls it. A dead PID is demoted via `isProcessAlive` in the `requireFreshArm` guard and `deriveListenerState`. Since `FRESH_ARM_GUARD_STATES` already includes `exited`, retaining the PID through `markExited` lets the guard correctly skip a duplicate while the old listener is still alive — closing the duplicate-creation window that `markArmIntent` PID-nulling opened (the dominant root cause).

The epoch makes the guarantee provable even if a duplicate listener still slips through (e.g. an `isProcessAlive` false-negative): the superseded listener has the stale epoch and is refused; worst case the message is **left queued** for the current listener, never consumed-and-dropped.

### Implementation Strategy
1. **Code fix + regression tests (US-001).**
   - `hooks/protocol/manifest.js`: add `lastListenerEpoch` (number) to the declared manifest fields; bump the field-count assertion; treat absent as `0`.
   - `hooks/actors.js`: `markArmed`/`touchHeartbeat` bump `lastListenerEpoch = (current || 0) + 1` and write it alongside `lastListenerPid` under the manifest lock ONLY on a genuine arm transition — i.e. when the arming PID differs from the current `lastListenerPid` OR no epoch exists yet. A heartbeat refresh from the SAME owning listener (same PID, already the owner) must NOT bump the epoch, otherwise the owning listener would invalidate its own captured epoch (the heartbeat timer calls `markArmed` every ~10s). The listener captures its granted epoch from its first `markArmed` and reuses it for the rest of its lifetime. `markArmIntent`: stop nulling `lastListenerPid`/`lastHeartbeatAt` (stamp `listenerState:'armed'` only). Audit confirms `markExited`/`markListenerExited` already does NOT null `lastListenerPid` today (it writes only `lastListenerExitedAt`/`listenerState`), so no change there — `markArmIntent` is the only normal-flow PID-nuller to fix; the `lastListenerPid: null` writes in the takeover manifests (recoverable-takeover path) are intentional and OUT OF SCOPE. Only a new `markArmed` overwrites `lastListenerPid` (F-006).
   - `hooks/mailbox.js`: `consumeMailbox` accepts `opts.listenerEpoch` (and keeps `opts.listenerPid`). IMPLEMENTATION NOTE (lock placement): the actual drain-commit that empties the queue is `writeJsonAtomic(mailboxPath, mailboxTemplate())` at ~:563, which today sits OUTSIDE the `withManifestLock` at ~:572. The epoch ownership check must GATE that mailbox-empty write — restructure so the sequence is: acquire `withManifestLock` (inside the existing `withMailboxLock`), read `manifest.lastListenerEpoch`, and if the caller's epoch is not current, return `[]` BEFORE writing any history row or emptying `mailbox.json`; only on a match proceed to write history + empty the mailbox + apply the manifest patch, all within that serialized block. Do NOT naively add the check only at the existing :572 patch site (the queue would already be emptied by :563). INERT-ON-UNSET rule: if `opts.listenerEpoch` is undefined OR `manifest.lastListenerEpoch` is undefined/0 (e.g. a `markArmed` epoch-write was lost to an EPERM retry-exhaustion), do NOT refuse — fall through to the normal drain (no false refusal). On a genuine mismatch, log `listener-orphan-consume-refused name=.. crew=.. callerPid=.. callerEpoch=.. manifestEpoch=..` and return `[]`.
   - `lib/listener-loop.js`: `deliver()` passes `{ sessionId, listenerPid, listenerEpoch }` using the loop's existing `listenerPid` variable (~:95) and the epoch the listener captured at `markArmed` (F-008).

Add the integration test to the `tests/run.js` serial denylist if it spawns subprocesses (F-007).
   - Full suite green: `cd ai-developer-toolkit/plugins/crews && node tests/run.js`.

## Scope

### In Scope
- The monotonic `lastListenerEpoch` ownership token + the `consumeMailbox` epoch ownership check under the manifest lock.
- The prevention layer: only a new `markArmed` writes `lastListenerPid`; `markArmIntent`/`markExited` do not null it.
- Threading `{ listenerPid, listenerEpoch }` from `deliver()` via the loop's existing seam.
- A deterministic unit test + an end-to-end integration test (asserting the real lost-notification observable) + updates to `tests/mark-arm-intent.test.js` and the manifest field-count test.
- The crews patch-release ceremony, including the codexu pointer-bump commit and the root AGENTS.md CI-invariant table.

### Out of Scope
- The broader Copilot `agentStop`-unreliability redesign (separate tracked work).
- The Windows `events.jsonl` ~100ms flush race (separate; only noted as an aggravator).
- Any change to the v2 report protocol, the proactive-routing producer in stop.js, or the report/outbox layer.
- A delivery-receipt/ack handshake protocol (rejected as too high-risk/high-surface; the epoch achieves the guarantee more cheaply).
- Reworking the Stop-hook opportunistic-consume path beyond a regression case (Mechanism B is adequately defended for leads via `decision:block`; the epoch check also protects the Stop-hook drain if `listenerEpoch` is threaded there, but that is optional hardening).

## Risk Areas
- **Dropping legitimate mail:** LOW — the epoch check only refuses when the caller is not the current-epoch listener. The current listener captured its epoch at its own `markArmed`, which equals `manifest.lastListenerEpoch` until a newer listener arms. If a listener's `markArmed` write failed (EPERM) leaving no epoch, the check must be inert (no false refusal). Verify.
- **Mail stuck forever (manifest points at a dead listener):** LOW/MEDIUM — if the current-epoch listener died without draining, the next legitimate arm bumps the epoch and becomes the owner, then drains the queued mail. Verify that a fresh arm after a dead current listener correctly takes ownership and drains (F-011 retry path), and that `deriveListenerState` demotes the dead PID so a new arm is allowed.
- **Live-listener retry after an orphan returns `[]`:** MEDIUM — the orphan holds then releases `withMailboxLock`; the current listener must get another `deliver()` trigger (poll backstop or its own `fs.watch`) to drain. Each subprocess has its own watcher, so the orphan returning `[]` does not consume the current listener's watch event. Confirm prompt re-delivery, not delivery-only-at-timeout (F-011).
- **`markArmIntent`/`markExited` leaving a stale dead PID:** acceptable — `deriveListenerState`/the guard demote on `isProcessAlive===false`; the next `markArmed` overwrites PID+epoch. Confirm no consumer treats a stale `lastListenerPid` as authoritative liveness without the `isProcessAlive` check (F-006).
- **Invariant regressions:** MUST re-run the full crews suite and specifically `mark-arm-intent.test.js`, `listener-redundant-arm-skip.test.js`, `stale-listener.test.js`, the 1.2.1 property tests, and the manifest field-count test. The `markArmIntent` and manifest-field changes touch load-bearing surfaces.
- **Conflict with `impl-d001-toolkit-guard`:** code = none (disjoint edit sites); version files + AGENTS.md + CHANGELOG = LOW (serialize, different sections). IMPL runs AFTER d001 ships and rebases onto the post-d001 toolkit main (record the base SHA — F-012).

## Acceptance Criteria
- `manifest.lastListenerEpoch` is declared in `hooks/protocol/manifest.js` (number; absent treated as `0`); the manifest field-count assertion is updated; `markArmed`/`touchHeartbeat` bump+record it on the arm transition (not on plain heartbeat ticks) under the manifest lock alongside `lastListenerPid`.
- `markArmIntent` no longer writes `lastListenerPid: null` (nor `lastHeartbeatAt: null`) in any branch; it stamps `listenerState:'armed'` only. `markExited` (and any dead-PID-clear path) does not null `lastListenerPid`; only a new listener's `markArmed` overwrites it. (Verified by updated `tests/mark-arm-intent.test.js` asserting the new contract.)
- `consumeMailbox` accepts `opts.listenerEpoch` (and `opts.listenerPid`) and, under the manifest lock atomically with the drain, refuses (returns `[]`, writes no mailbox-history row, leaves `mailbox.json` unchanged, appends `listener-orphan-consume-refused …` to crews.log) when the caller's epoch is not `manifest.lastListenerEpoch`. When epoch matches, it drains normally (commits `consumedAt`, advances `lastReviewRequiredSeq`).
- `lib/listener-loop.js` `deliver()` passes `{ sessionId, listenerPid, listenerEpoch }` using the loop's existing `listenerPid` variable and the epoch captured at `markArmed`.
- Deterministic unit test `tests/consume-mailbox-epoch-fence.test.js`: seed `manifest.lastListenerEpoch`/`lastListenerPid`, append one message, call `consumeMailbox(..., {sessionId, listenerPid, listenerEpoch: <stale>})` → asserts `[]`, no new mailbox-history row (count unchanged), `mailbox.json` unchanged, `listener-orphan-consume-refused` logged; then call with the current epoch → asserts the one message drains and exactly one new `consumedAt` history row appears; plus an inert-on-unset case where `opts.listenerEpoch` is undefined OR `manifest.lastListenerEpoch` is unset/0 → drains normally (no false refusal) (F-007, F-010).
- End-to-end integration test `tests/integration/proactive-report-silent-loss-race.test.js`: with two same-session listeners (current-epoch + a stale-epoch orphan) and ONE queued proactive `done`, asserts (a) the orphan does NOT emit a `{type:messages}` envelope (returns `[]`/exits without delivering); (b) the current-epoch listener emits EXACTLY ONE `{type:messages,count:1}` delivery; (c) mailbox-history has exactly one `consumedAt` row (from the current listener), none from the orphan; (d) `markArmIntent` did not clear `lastListenerPid`. Added to the `tests/run.js` serial denylist if it spawns subprocesses (F-005, F-007, F-010).
- Full crews suite passes: `cd ai-developer-toolkit/plugins/crews && node tests/run.js` (all green, under the documented Windows ceiling). `node --check` passes on every changed `.js` file.
- Release: crews version bumped via `node scripts/bump-version.js <next>`; `node tests/version.test.js` passes (6 stamps + the test); crews `CHANGELOG.md` has a `## <next> - <date>` section; crews `AGENTS.md` has a new section AND the existing v1.2.12 section is amended to reflect the no-null `markArmIntent` contract (F-009); the 3 marketplace indexes carry `<next>`.
- Two-commit ship: (1) a single `ai-developer-toolkit` submodule commit with all crews changes; (2) a single codexu parent commit recording the new gitlink AND bumping the root `D:/harness-efforts/codexu/AGENTS.md` active-plugin-versions table crews row to `<next>` (F-001, F-004). The root worktree shows the updated gitlink + table together.
